text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz has dismissed Foreign Trade Minister Jacek Buchacz for promoting unclear capital operations between the state and private sector which was outlined in a Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) report.

- Farming modernisation and land purchase loans granted by the Farming Modernisation and Restructuring Agency (ARiMR) are becoming more and more popular as ARiMR subsidizes the credits, the Agency president Henryk Antosik said.
- Poland is Europe's fourth biggest apple producer with annual crops ranging from 1.5 to 1.7 million tonnes, 50 percent of which are sold abroad.

- Wloclawek-based Delecta food concentrates maker will invest $10 million in ready-made goods and raw materials storage capacity and modern blending equipment. The firm considers inviting a strategic investor and listing its stock on the Warsaw bourse.
- Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko granted Tarnowskie Gory chemical plant, now under liquidation, a 600,000 zloty subsidy to finance the plant's environmental protection scheme.
NOWA EUROPA
- Exxon Corp and Shell will form a Polish Petroleum Development Company to explore for oil and gas in Poland, their representatives said.
- Polski Bank Rozwoju (PBR) bank will issue up to $75 million of Eurobonds, placing it privately by mid-November. PBR's issue will be the third Eurobond issue by a Polish bank.
- Over a dozen Polish banks expect another interest rate cut on deposits and credits, a Nowa Europa survey said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- South Korea's LG Group plans to invest up to $500 million in Poland in the coming four years. This month the group will pay $50 million for the Lodz-based Petrobank shares it contracted for in June this year.

- Ciech chemical foreign trade company directors are against their firm's participation in the Chemia Polska Ciech Holding promoted by Poland's foreign trade ministry. "Any attempts to make us join the new body are totally unacceptable," Ciech's supervisory board president Jerzy Reszke said.

- Era GSM digital cellular phone network controlled by Polska Telefonia Cyfrowa (PTC) company will start operating on September 16 this year while its main competitor GSM Plus, controlled by Polkomtel, will start in October.
- Curtis Electronics will introduce its cheapest television receiver priced at 777 zlotys and aimed at low income buyers.

- South Korea's Kyungbang concern has bought an 80 percent stake in the Lodz-based Fonica sound system and electric equipment maker from the Industrial Development Agency (ARP). Kyungbang promised to keep the present level of employment and invest $1.5 million in Fonica's modernisation.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY
- Poznan court has passed the Hestja SA insurance agency bankruptcy verdict. The court appointed the Warsaw-based insurer Polisa SA as the bankrupt company's receiver.
- Around 2,000 companies from 33 countries will exhibit their products at the Poznan Polagra'96 food products international fair to take place later in September.
PARKIET - Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) bank and Allied Irish Banks will set up mutual investment funds and an asset management company in Poland, the banks' representatives said.
- Deloitte & Touche international auditing company and the Polish Providum auditing firm have merged after two years of talks, Deloitte & Touche Polish branch president Leslaw Paga said.
- In the first eight months of 1996 the Stomil Olsztyn tyre maker has reported record 456.6 million zlotys revenues. In the coming three years the company plans to invest $150 million.
- The listed Bank Rozwoju Exportu (BRE), export development bank, has bought a 26 percent stake in Radom-based Bank Energetyki, an energy sector bank.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
